profile.subseg: Graphite electrodes; Needle coke; Electric arc furnace steel; Carbon footprint compliance
profile.themes: CBAM-driven steel decarbonization; Electric arc furnace capacity expansion; Needle coke supply constraints; Geopolitical trade regionalization

deepdive.sec: Graphite Electrodes & Electric Arc Furnace Steel Transition

bull_bear.body: No debt; INR 792cr treasury; final dividend of INR 3.4/share recommended; GrafTech stake held as strategic long-term hedge against needle coke supply risk
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Needle coke supply tightness if battery demand surges; geopolitical disruption in Middle East shipping lanes; CBAM implementation delays; competitor price undercutting; FX volatility on unrealized gains/losses
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident, strategic, and long-term oriented; emphasized structural demand shift, not cyclicality; dismissed short-term noise; reinforced commitment to GrafTech investment as hedge; tone on pricing is assertive but pragmatic
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: HEG’s 90%+ utilization is the highest globally — competitors run at 60-65%; GrafTech stake is not speculative but a strategic hedge against needle coke scarcity; Middle East customers are willing to pay $300/ton extra in road freight to avoid plant shutdowns; no new needle coke capacity added globally in 70+ years
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- The restructuring enables each entity to raise capital independently for growth, with HEG Greentech to be listed separately.
- Steady hydro cash flows (~â¹300+ Cr annually) are used to self-fund the anode and graphene growth roadmap, supplemented by equity and debt.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: Core graphite electrodes: 94% capacity utilization, 20% volume growth; TACC (Greentech): pilot plant complete, sampling with LG/Panasonic/CATL ongoing, 40-60% utilization expected in Year 1; no tech bottlenecks
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- The Greentech platform is positioned as an integrated clean-tech entity with autonomy across cell chemistries, combining manufacturing, R&D, and green power generation.
- The restructuring unlocks value by separating the legacy graphite electrode business from the high-growth Greentech business, enabling pure-play focus and independent capital raising.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Restructuring] The Composite Scheme of Arrangement will demerge the Greentech business into a separately listed entity, HEG Greentech, with shareholders receiving shares in the new company.
- [R&D Partnerships] MOU signed with Nobel laureate Prof. K. Novoselov for graphene; partnerships with AcSIR, NUS, NCCBM, CSIR-CRRI, and Berger Paints for material validation and commercialization.
- [Offtake Discussions] Advanced non-binding offtake discussions for anode materials exceed 40,000 MT with global OEMs and cell makers, including a European legacy automotive OEM and a North American global automotive company.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: revenue: +19% YoY (INR 2,569cr vs 2,153cr); EBITDA: +28% YoY (INR 497cr vs 388cr), margin: +200bps to 19%; PAT (rptd): -189cr (Q4) due to $40cr FX loss + GrafTech fair value drag; PAT (normalized): +78% YoY (INR 181cr vs 101cr); order book: booked till Sept 2026; net debt: INR 0 (treasury: INR 792cr)
latest_quarter.title: Financial scorecard

latest_quarter.body: EBITDA margin expanded to 19% on volume leverage and cost discipline; needle coke costs covered till Sept 2026; energy/freight inflation partially offset by rupee depreciation (net positive); Middle East freight spike ($20 to $300/ton) managed via force majeure
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: revenue growth: implied 15-20% FY27 (based on 100Kt capacity + price hikes); margin: stable at 18-20% post-price adjustments; order inflow: strong demand from EU/US/East Asia; capex/commissioning: 15Kt expansion (total 115Kt) to be commissioned by early 2028
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Booked through September 2026; Middle East orders deferred but not canceled; new contracts post-Sept include price increases
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: 115Kt expansion (2028) positions HEG as only global player with announced capacity growth; potential to capture 200Kt incremental electrode demand by 2030 from non-China EAF build-out
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: HEG delivered strong volume-driven revenue and EBITDA growth in FY26, supported by 90%+ capacity utilization and cost leadership, while structural tailwinds from global CBAM policies and 100M+ ton of new EAF capacity by 2030 create a multi-year demand inflection; near-term earnings were distorted by $40cr unrealized FX losses and temporary mix shifts, but pricing power is now being activated post-September contracts.

open.item: Management expects electrode prices to firm up only once industry utilisation crosses 80-85%, likely two-three quarters away; prices believed to be at the bottom now.
Total anode plant capex is around Rs. 1,850 crores, with a little over Rs. 100 crores spent so far and near-100% commitment planned within FY26, funded by a mix of debt and equity.
RePlus BESS EPC business to expand assembly capacity from 1 GWh to 6 GWh by Q1 FY27.
Of the ~Rs. 1,200 crores treasury, Rs. 830 crores is allocated to TACC (anode/greentech) and the remainder to the graphite entity at demerger.
Countervailing and anti-dumping duties in US against Indian and Chinese graphite electrode imports; outcome expected by September 2026.
Composite scheme of arrangement expected to be approved by NCLT sometime in Q2 FY27, subject to approvals.
Board recommended a final dividend of INR 3.4 per equity share (face value INR 2), subject to shareholder approval.
Management expects EBITDA margin to be around 20% for Q1 and Q2 FY27.
First 200 MWh IPP (BESS+Solar) project expected operational by Q2 FY27, with an additional 1,000 MW/2,000 MWh tender targeted for commissioning by Q2 FY28.
HEG is offering increased prices for uncommitted volumes; aiming for price increase in H2FY27 to protect and improve margins.
TACC (HEG Greentech) aims for 40% to 60% capacity utilization in the first year after commissioning in April 2026.
HEG Greentech EBITDA expected to at least double in FY27 versus FY26 (FY26 being Rs. 200-225 crores).
Anode project is expected to deliver EBITDA margins in the range of about 35-40% with encouraging IRR.
Anode plant (20,000 tons) production to start from 2027, with anode revenue flowing from Q4 FY27 once commissioned.
Combined capex cash outflow (anode plus electrode expansion) is expected to be around Rs. 1,000 crores this year and next, likely funded with some interim debt.
HEG's next expansion to 115,000 tons is likely to be operational by early 2028.
About 20 million tons of new EAF capacity expected to be added in CY2026-27, translating to roughly 30,000 tons of incremental electrode demand.
Anode plant starts at 20,000 tons but management hopes to at least double capacity at the same location in the next 4-5 years, targeting an India market of 100,000-140,000 tons by 2030.
Over 100 million tons of new EAF capacity announced with 65-70 mt due to start between 2025-26 and H1 2027, driving 150,000-200,000 tons incremental electrode demand.
Management reaffirms commitment to the long-term investment in GrafTech, anchored in structural fundamentals.

revisions.item: Management expects electrode prices to firm up only once industry utilisation crosses 80-85%, likely two-three quarters away; prices believed to be at the bottom now.
HEG Greentech EBITDA expected to at least double in FY27 versus FY26 (FY26 being Rs. 200-225 crores).
Management expects margins in Q3 and Q4 FY26 to remain similar to the last two quarters, with no margin improvement in Q3 as prices and needle coke stay flat.
Management expects full-year FY27 EBITDA margin to be above 20%.

verdicts.item: Management expects full-year FY27 EBITDA margin to be above 20%.
About 11 million tons of new greenfield EAF capacity commissioned in last 18 months, with another 25-30 million tons expected in the next 18 months (~35-40 mt total).
verdicts.note: Management says 'about 20 million tons of new Greenfield electric arc furnaces have already been commissioned in the last 12 to 18 months... an additional 60 million tons... by 2028, and another about…

verdicts.item: Recent 10% US import duty flagged as a headwind; if not withdrawn it will have some impact, though expected limited given diversified sales; key date is 9th July.
verdicts.note: expired: no update 3Q past horizon Q1FY26

verdicts.item: Graphite anode plant commissioning timeline is now April 2027.
verdicts.note: Management confirms: 'There is no change in the plant commissioning date from April' (April 2027), matching the promised timeline.

verdicts.item: New expansion from 100,000 to 115,000 tons electrode capacity announced, requiring ~Rs. 650 crores capex, to be completed in 2.5 years with production expected in January-March 2028.
verdicts.note: Management confirms: 'we have already announced our next expansion to 115,000 tons, which is likely to be operational by early 2028.'

verdicts.item: Q1 FY26 capacity utilisation was 90%+ on 100,000 tons; management guides to ~85% for the balance three quarters of FY26.
verdicts.note: Management states 'averaging more than 90% for the whole year, as well as the past three, four immediate quarters,' exceeding the ~85% guidance for balance FY26.

verdicts.item: Anode plant (20,000 tons) to be operational by March 2027; total capex Rs. 1,800-1,900 crores with Rs. 750 crores HEG equity and the rest via financial closure/debt.
verdicts.note: Management confirms commissioning in April 2027, not March 2027. 'There is no change in the plant commissioning date from April.'

verdicts.item: Graphite anode plant (20,000 tons, 105 acres in Dewas) targeted to be fully operational by September 2026.
verdicts.note: Management states 'There is no change in the plant commissioning date from April' (April 2027), confirming the prior slipped status from Sep 2026.

verdicts.item: FY25 capacity utilisation was close to 80% on 100,000 tons; management hopes to maintain or slightly increase this in FY26.
verdicts.note: Management states 'averaging more than 90% for the whole year' on the expanded 100,000 tons capacity, exceeding the ~80% target.

verdicts.item: Roughly 100 million tons of new EAF capacity expected over the next few years (11-12 mt already in, 20-25 mt within this and next year), driving 150,000-200,000 tons annual electrode demand by 2030.
verdicts.note: Management states 'incremental electrode demand of around 200,000 tons by 2030, excluding China,' which is within the 150,000-200,000 range. However, the breakdown of 11-12 mt already in and 20-25 mt …

verdicts.item: Announced 15,000-ton electrode expansion (to 115,000 tons) with Rs. 650 crores capex, to be completed by end of 2027 and ready for production in Q1 calendar 2028.
verdicts.note: Management confirms: 'Construction of the additional 15,000 tons expansion is progressing as planned, and we continue to target completion by early 2028.'

verdicts.item: Post consolidation of hydro assets, HEG Greentech consolidated EBITDA is between Rs. 275-300 crores based on today's numbers.
verdicts.note: expired: no update 2Q past horizon Q2FY26

wtt.summary: 35% guidance hit (5 chains); 0/2 projects on-time; 3 guidance revision(s); 2 expired; 16% theme consistency (info)
wtt.tone_latest: Confident and optimistic about long-term structural demand, while acknowledging near-term headwinds from geopolitical tensions and cost pressures. Management owned the Q4 loss by transparently attributing it to unrealized FX and fair-value losses, and emphasized that operating margins remain intact.
